---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines
---

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS. It starts automatically for promotional offers with no active delivery, shows the customer’s full address on Lock Screen, labels a 40-minute-old estimate Now, keeps displaying Delivered forever and puts a complete shopping catalog inside expanded content.

# Apple HIG: Select the system surface before designing its content

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Decide whether the task needs a widget, ongoing Live Activity, notification, Siri snippet or another system-owned surface. Enter that surface’s procedure before fitting an app screen into it.
2. Specify the useful glance/action, data freshness and deep-link destination. Respect the surface’s update, interaction, presentation and privacy constraints rather than assuming full-app behavior.
3. Cover the relevant family/size, appearance, redaction, account and unavailable-data contexts. Shared surfaces require explicit decisions about whose information may be visible.
4. Deliver a surface/content/state contract and preview/check matrix; preserve documented platform support and unresolved source conflicts.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

name: apple-hig-live-activities
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting bounded live-event progress, compact and expanded presentations, updates, actions, and ending behavior.
---

# Give the live event a start and an end

Read [the Live Activities guide](../../references/live-activities.md). This workflow is application advice; destination layouts and interaction support differ.

Inspect event duration/start/end, update source, sensitivity, destinations, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Decide whether the information is a bounded task with frequent changes or ordinary periodic widget data. Record real update/termination signals; a timer mockup is not a delivery guarantee.

Design essential iPhone compact/minimal/expanded/Lock Screen content first, retaining identity/relative positions as it expands, then tailor other destinations. Keep minimal content informative rather than a static logo. Use supported background customization only in Lock Screen, with appropriate dark/tint/Always On contrast. Favor one essential direct action and precise deep links. Protect sensitive content, omit promotion, update only changed content, and alert only for crucial updates without duplicate pushes. End immediately when the task ends and choose a useful short retained summary, not indefinite activity.

Implement the lifecycle/layouts or provide event-state/destination specifications; review exact lifecycle, privacy, or missing-presentation defects. StandBy needs scaling/red-mode checks. Watch custom layout can share CarPlay use, where controls are disabled. Mac activation uses iPhone Mirroring; tvOS/visionOS are unsupported. Do not reuse a control-dependent watch layout as a driving workflow.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a courier activity runs after delivery, exposes a full address, and requires Pause on CarPlay. Decision: the task is over, private information is excessive, and driving controls are disabled. After: end at delivery, retain a brief safe summary where allowed, show only necessary destination context, and make CarPlay status useful without interaction.

Deliver the artifact, state lifecycle, update/alert policy, all relevant presentations, and destinations. Verify multiple activities/minimal state, completion, stale updates, red/Always On, and control-disabled destinations. Fail for unbounded lifecycle, misleading status, duplicate alerts, or unsupported interaction. Actual push delivery/native rendering/device behavior requires execution evidence.

Load [widgets](../apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md) for periodic data, [notifications](../apple-hig-notifications/SKILL.md) for separate events, or [app-shortcuts](../apple-hig-app-shortcuts/SKILL.md) for relevant initiation.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

name: apple-hig-privacy
description: Use when designing or reviewing permission timing, purpose strings, pre-permission explanations, tracking requests, data minimization, or private platform inputs.
---

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

For health-related work, finish the domain decisions as well as the permission
sequence. Read [CareKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-carekit/SKILL.md)
for care plans, scheduled treatment tasks, or symptom/event recording;
[HealthKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-healthkit/SKILL.md)
for health-data access and sharing; and
[ResearchKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-researchkit/SKILL.md)
for study participation and research consent. These experience procedures help
choose task, data, and consent behavior in the existing stack; consulting a
framework-named topic does not require adopting that SDK. General privacy,
language, and accessibility guidance alone does not resolve those domain choices.

# Live Activities Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Anatomy](#Anatomy) - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Presentation](#Presentation) - [CarPlay](#CarPlay) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) Live Activities track a bounded task or event through frequent updates over a few hours. They begin on iPhone or iPad and can appear on the Lock/Home Screen, Dynamic Island and StandBy, paired Mac menu bar, Apple Watch Smart Stack, and CarPlay Dashboard. ## Anatomy Support compact, minimal, expanded, and Lock Screen presentations. The system composes these for available space and devices. ### Compact A single Dynamic Island activity uses separate leading/trailing elements around the TrueDepth camera. ### Minimal Multiple activities use compact circular/oval treatments, up to three where supported: one attached and others detached. Tap opens the app; hold expands. ### Expanded Holding compact/minimal content reveals a larger presentation. ### Lock Screen A bottom banner uses a layout related to expanded. On devices without Dynamic Island, essential update alerts can briefly overlay this banner on Home or another app. ### StandBy Minimal content expands on tap to a Lock Screen layout scaled 2×. A custom background extends across the screen. ## Best practices Use tasks with clear starts and ends, ideally no more than 8 hours. Show only immediately useful information, with details in the app. Exclude ads and promotions. Avoid exposed sensitive content; summarize or redact and offer app access/configuration. Match app identity across appearances; a logo mark can appear without a container, but do not use the full app icon. Do not draw attention to Dynamic Island from inside the app. Use legible large text, generally medium weight or stronger. ### Creating Live Activity layouts Adapt to actual screens and scale factors. Keep layout only as large as content needs. For limited-width Dynamic Island contexts, fit compact/minimal content within a 28-pt circle with abbreviations or graphics; use leading-only when a meaningful trailing version cannot fit. Favor familiar templates, even concentric margins, and container-relative corner radii. Inset groups or use a thick dividing line instead of extending content to edges. A blurred drawing-tool preview can help align angular content within rounded corners. Adjust Lock Screen/expanded height as available information grows or shrinks. ### Choosing colors Only Lock Screen permits custom background colors; compact, minimal, and expanded backgrounds are system-controlled. Dynamic Island is opaque black, so meaningful bold foreground color can express identity. Match its dark-background keyline to related content. Check custom Lock Screen contrast in both appearances and reduced-luminance Always On. ### Adding transitions and animating content updates Animations can last at most 2 seconds and are not played in reduced-luminance Always On. Use numeric changes, fades, scale, or movement to explain updates. Preserve existing elements as layout grows rather than removing/readding everything. Avoid transition collisions; animate a moved item and fade other list elements when needed. ### Offering interactivity Deep-link to the relevant task. Favor one essential button or toggle for a direct action, pause/resume, or response to meaningful progress, preserving space for status and reducing accidental activation. ### Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity Begin at expected moments, including automatic starts for followed events, with an easy opt-out in the corresponding app view. Offer an App Shortcut when useful. Update only for changed content. Alert only for crucial updates and avoid a parallel push for the same information. Prefer one dynamically changing activity for related simultaneous events. Choose a shorter useful summary lifetime, commonly 15–30 minutes, proportional to the activity. ## Presentation Design the iPhone presentations first, then tailor layouts for StandBy, watch, and driving while supporting every destination. ### Compact presentation Show essential changing data. Make both halves read as one through coherent color/type and balanced widths. Fit snugly against the camera without extra inner padding or unnecessary status-bar obstruction; shorten units or precision as needed. Both halves should deep-link to the same relevant app screen. ### Minimal presentation Preserve recognition while conveying current information instead of only a static logo. ### Expanded presentation Expand predictably from the smaller layout, retaining relative positions and fitting content close to the camera rather than leaving unused gaps. ### Lock Screen presentation Create a distinct task layout rather than copying notification structure. Use restrained tint/background customization to fit personalized wallpapers. Verify contrast in both appearances and Always On, including the system-generated dismiss-button color; override its foreground if needed. Standard margins are 14 pt, with tighter spacing only when content grouping needs it. ### StandBy presentation Supply assets and, where useful, a custom layout for the larger scale. The default background blends with the bezel and surroundings and permits slightly more content scale. Preserve margins so expansion does not crop graphics, and test the red-tinted Night Mode. ## CarPlay The default combines compact halves. A supplemental small family can support larger type and more information. Its custom layout is also used on watch, but CarPlay disables buttons and toggles; driving-oriented activities should prioritize timely content over those controls. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS or iPadOS rules are specified. Live Activities are unsupported in tvOS and visionOS. ### macOS Paired Mac menu-bar presentations use compact/minimal/expanded styles. Activation opens the app through iPhone Mirroring. ### watchOS The activity appears atop the paired watch's Smart Stack, combining compact halves by default. Tap opens a watch app when available; otherwise it opens a full-screen view with a paired-iPhone launch button. A custom layout can improve essential progress, changes, and controls, but consider its shared use in CarPlay where interaction is disabled. ## Specifications These source dimensions are design guidance in points; # Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. item.text: The proposal has five verified problems: promotional use without an active delivery, address exposure, a stale estimate labeled “Now,” indefinite completion display, and a full catalog in expanded content. I’ll specify when the activity starts and ends, how stale data appears, and what stays in the app.

/bin/bash -lc "cat > result.md <<'EOF'
# Delivery Live Activity review

Decision: revise before implementation. The five findings below are verified against the written proposal in "'`interface.md`, not against a running interface. Ranking reflects privacy exposure and harm to delivery decisions, followed by lifecycle and scope. This is an iOS iPhone Lock Screen review; no framework or Apple SDK is assumed.

## Ranked findings and decisions

| Rank | Verified proposal | Effect and source-backed finding | Corrected behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — High | Shows the customer’s full address on Lock Screen. | Exposes sensitive destination information to nearby people. Live Activities guidance says to avoid exposing sensitive content and summarize or redact it. | Omit the full address from every activity presentation and its display payload. Show “Your delivery”; open the corresponding order in the app for private destination details. |
| 2 — High | Labels a 40-minute-old estimate “Now.” | Presents an old prediction as current, misleading a person deciding whether to meet the courier. The topic procedure explicitly fails misleading status; the guide calls for immediately useful, changing information. | Show “Estimate unavailable · Updated 40 min ago”; retain the last confirmed delivery phase with its age. Never infer arrival from an elapsed estimate. |
| 3 — High | Starts automatically for promotional offers with no active delivery. | There is no bounded delivery task, and promotion is explicitly excluded from Live Activities. Automatic initiation itself is not the defect: expected automatic starts for followed events are allowed. | Start only for a real, active delivery at an expected moment, with an easy opt-out in that order’s app view. Keep offers outside this surface. |
| 4 — Medium | Keeps displaying “Delivered” forever. | An ended task must end immediately; indefinite retention defeats the bounded lifecycle. | End on confirmed delivery, remove from active presentations, and request a short Lock Screen completion summary, then removal. Choose 15 minutes as this product’s retention policy. |
| 5 — Medium | Puts a complete shopping catalog inside expanded content. | Displaces delivery status with nonessential app content. The guide calls for immediately useful information with details in the app. A catalog need not be advertising to be inappropriate here. | Expanded content shows delivery identity, confirmed phase, current estimate or stale-data explanation, and update age. Activity activation opens that order; catalog browsing remains in the app. |

Source for findings 1, 3, and 5: [Live Activities — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices). Sources for finding 2: the installed Live Activities topic procedure and [Compact presentation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Compact-presentation). Source for finding 4 and expected initiation: [Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity). These are links supplied by local guidance; no website was accessed.

## Corrected contract

The following thresholds and wording are product decisions, not Apple-mandated values. Choose a conservative five-minute estimate freshness limit until the delivery service supplies a validated expiry. Honor any earlier service expiry. Do not promise a delivery update cadence that has not been established.

```text
state = absent | active | ended
input = orderId, eventVersion, confirmedPhase, observedAt,
        estimateWindow?, estimateObservedAt?, serviceValidUntil?, terminalAt?

on delivery event:
  accept only an event for this order with a newer authoritative version
  if confirmedPhase is delivered or cancelled:
    end activity immediately, once
    request safe final summary removal at terminalAt + 15 minutes
    discard later nonterminal events for this delivery
  else if delivery is active and tracking is allowed and not opted out:
    start at the expected order-tracking moment, or update changed content
  else:
    do not create an activity

render(now):
  never include address, catalog, offers, or other private order details
  if ended: show "Delivered" or "Delivery cancelled" with terminal time
  if active:
    show last confirmed phase and the age of that confirmation
    estimateExpiry = min(estimateObservedAt + 5 minutes,
                         serviceValidUntil if supplied)
    if estimate exists and now < estimateExpiry and window has not passed:
      show "Estimated arrival <window>" and estimate update age
    else:
      show "Estimate unavailable" and last estimate update age if known
  never map an expired estimate to "Now" or "Delivered"
  if timestamps are absent or invalid: show "Update time unavailable"

on activation:
  open corresponding order tracking in app, subject to normal access controls
on opt-out in order view:
  end activity and suppress automatic restart for this delivery
```

Recompute freshness when time crosses the expiry even without another delivery event. The eventual implementation must arrange supported expiry/rendering behavior; this pseudocode alone does not prove that a remotely displayed estimate will change on time. If expiry cannot be reliably represented, omit the estimate rather than retain a claim of current arrival. On termination, request the end and removal immediately even if an event arrives late; do not start a new 15-minute window from late receipt. System dismissal can remove the summary earlier.

Update only changed information. Alert only for crucial changes, such as a confirmed arrival requiring attention; do not send a duplicate push for the same update. Backend event delivery, ordering, and terminal signals remain implementation dependencies.

### Presentation and destination decisions

| Presentation | Essential content and behavior |
|---|---|
| Lock Screen | “Your delivery,” last confirmed phase, estimate or freshness explanation. Brief completion summary after ending. Distinct task layout; standard 14 pt margins from the local guide, adjusting only for justified grouping. |
| Expanded | Same identity and relative positions as smaller presentations, with room for update ages. No catalog. |
| Compact | Delivery symbol/identity and short changing estimate or stale-status indicator. Both halves open the same order. |
| Minimal / multiple activities | Recognizable delivery symbol plus meaningful current state, such as a stale indicator; never a static logo alone. |

No explicit buttons, toggles, catalog controls, or interaction mechanics were supplied, so none can be declared defective. Use the activity’s relevant-order deep link; no new direct-action control is necessary for this correction. These compact/minimal provisions cover related iPhone presentations without claiming rendered support.

For eventual destination coverage, check StandBy scaling and red Night Mode, watch status, and CarPlay status with controls disabled; paired Mac activation follows the local guide’s iPhone Mirroring model. No separate destination implementation is claimed here. Sources: [Presentation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Presentation), [Offering interactivity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Offering-interactivity), and [CarPlay](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#CarPlay).

### Data-purpose and privacy decisions

| Data | Purpose | Activity exposure |
|---|---|---|
| Internal order identifier | Route to the correct order and reject unrelated events | Routing metadata; no customer-identifying display required |
| Phase, estimate, observation time | Delivery progress and truthful freshness | Show only necessary status |
| Full address | Fulfillment and private order details | Exclude from activity display payload; access within the app |
| Catalog and promotional offers | Shopping | Exclude from activity |

No extra permission request is specified: the brief supplies no collection or authorization flow to audit. Retain existing authorized fulfillment data handling; this review does not establish that consent, storage, transfers, authentication, or privacy disclosures are correct. Data minimization is supported by [Privacy — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices); Lock Screen exposure is addressed directly by Live Activities guidance.

## Worked before/after

Illustrative fixture, not production data: at 12:40 a delivery remains last confirmed “On the way.” Its estimate was observed at 12:00 and predicted 12:05–12:15.

| Moment | Proposed behavior | Corrected behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Promotional offer, no delivery | Activity starts. | No activity. Offer stays outside the delivery surface. |
| Active delivery at 12:40 | Full address, “Now,” expanded catalog. | “Your delivery · On the way (last confirmed 40 min ago) · Estimate unavailable · Estimate updated 40 min ago.” No address or catalog. Activation opens this order. |
| Authoritative delivery event at 12:43 | “Delivered” persists forever. | End at 12:43. Lock Screen may retain “Delivered at 12:43” until requested removal at 12:58; active Dynamic Island presentation is removed. |
| Late “On the way” event after 12:43 | Unspecified. | Ignore older/nonterminal event; do not reopen the completed activity. |

## Acceptance checks and evidence status

**Passed — static audit only:** read the supplied proposal; identified five explicit behaviors and tied each to a correction; corrected specification excludes private destination text and shopping content and defines freshness, termination, and relevant-order routing. The worked example satisfies the written contract by inspection. No pseudocode was executed.

**Failed — supplied proposal by textual inspection:** all five ranked findings. These are specification failures, not observed runtime failures.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance checks:**

- A promotion without an active delivery creates nothing; an expected active-delivery start honors opt-out. Repeated events do not create duplicate activities or restart opted-out tracking.
- A fresh estimate is labeled estimated; at the earlier expiry boundary it becomes unavailable. At 40 minutes old it never says “Now.” Missing times, passed windows, loss of updates, and invalid timestamps cannot produce false arrival or completion.
- Confirmed delivery/cancellation ends immediately. A summary requests removal at terminal time plus 15 minutes, including late terminal events. Older updates cannot reverse completion.
- Every presentation excludes the full address, catalog, and offers; relevant-order activation respects app access controls. Inspect payloads and redacted states, including account changes.
- Changed-content updates and crucial alerts avoid duplicate push alerts; verify actual delivery and offline/reconnection behavior.
- Render on representative iPhones with and without Dynamic Island, multiple activities, long/localized text, and larger text settings. Check clipping, identity continuity, and meaningful minimal content. Test light/dark wallpaper contrast, Always On including dismiss control, and StandBy red mode. No contrast, typography, accessibility, or geometry defect is inferred from this text-only brief.
- Where destinations are delivered, verify watch/CarPlay status without required controls and paired Mac routing. Device, native rendering, assistive-technology behavior, SDK compilation, and server update delivery require actual execution evidence.

## Evidence limits and route record

Only `interface.md` and installed instructions/guides were used. No screenshots, source implementation, device, GUI, SDK, backend trace, or accessibility execution was available. The proposal omits actual update sources, timestamps, opt-out behavior, supported device/OS matrix, layouts, permission flow, and service guarantees. These omissions are open implementation questions, not additional verified violations.

Read sequence: installed `apple-hig/SKILL.md`; System experiences family; relevant rows of `references/topic-index.md`; Live Activities topic procedure; Foundations family; Privacy topic procedure; then the Live Activities and Privacy source guides. All paths resolved under `.agents/skills/apple-hig/`; each file was read with a separate `cat` or `rg` command. This routes the lifecycle, surface, and explicit privacy concerns without treating collection-permission guidance as proof of a Lock Screen authorization defect.

The installed guides identify a 2026-10-25 snapshot/retrieval date and are independent, derived guidance. Official links above are attribution, not live verification. No source conflict was encountered. The local guide says “ideally no more than 8 hours,” allows up to four hours of retained completion on specified surfaces, and recommends a shorter useful summary, commonly 15–30 minutes. These qualifications do not authorize indefinite display; this design selects 15 minutes without inventing an SDK limit or universal HIG requirement.
EOF'
